anchorData:
RAW DATA (same 20 learners, listed in the order the learners were given; learner numbers 1-20 follow this order, so learner 7 scored 95 in Subject 1 and 60 in Subject 2). Subject 1: 72, 85, 90, 67, 78, 81, 95, 88, 74, 69, 82, 76, 91, 84, 77, 70, 89, 73, 80, 86. Subject 2: 35, 42, 27, 58, 44, 31, 60, 29, 15, 30, 32, 51, 60, 11, 13, 32, 23, 18, 21, 45. Both sets have n = 20.

ASCENDING ORDER. Subject 1: 67, 69, 70, 72, 73, 74, 76, 77, 78, 80, 81, 82, 84, 85, 86, 88, 89, 90, 91, 95. Subject 2: 11, 13, 15, 18, 21, 23, 27, 29, 30, 31, 32, 32, 35, 42, 44, 45, 51, 58, 60, 60.

PASS MARK = 50 marks out of 100 (class agreement). Subject 1: 20 of 20 pass (lowest 67). Subject 2: 4 of 20 pass (51, 58, 60, 60) and 16 of 20 fail; 7 learners scored 40 or more.

UNGROUPED FREQUENCIES. Subject 1: every score occurs exactly once (20 different values, so no mode). Subject 2: 32 occurs twice and 60 occurs twice, every other score once (18 different values; modes 32 and 60, bimodal).

GROUPED FREQUENCY TABLE (common class width 10, classes written 10-19, 20-29, ..., 90-99; class boundaries 9.5-19.5, 19.5-29.5, ..., 89.5-99.5; midpoints 14.5, 24.5, 34.5, 44.5, 54.5, 64.5, 74.5, 84.5, 94.5). Frequencies for Subject 1 / Subject 2: 10-19: 0 / 4; 20-29: 0 / 4; 30-39: 0 / 5; 40-49: 0 / 3; 50-59: 0 / 2; 60-69: 2 / 2; 70-79: 7 / 0; 80-89: 8 / 0; 90-99: 3 / 0. Totals 20 / 20.

Subject 2 working (nonzero classes): 10-19 has 11, 13, 15, 18; 20-29 has 21, 23, 27, 29; 30-39 has 30, 31, 32, 32, 35; 40-49 has 42, 44, 45; 50-59 has 51, 58; 60-69 has 60, 60. Subject 1 working: 60-69 has 67, 69; 70-79 has 70, 72, 73, 74, 76, 77, 78; 80-89 has 80, 81, 82, 84, 85, 86, 88, 89; 90-99 has 90, 91, 95.

UNGROUPED MEASURES (exact). Subject 1: sum = 1607, mean = 1607/20 = 80.35, median = (80+81)/2 = 80.5, mode = none, range = 95-67 = 28, Q1 = 73.5, Q3 = 87, IQR = 13.5. Subject 2: sum = 677, mean = 677/20 = 33.85, median = (31+32)/2 = 31.5, modes = 32 and 60, range = 60-11 = 49, Q1 = 22, Q3 = 44.5, IQR = 22.5.

GROUPED ESTIMATES. Mean by midpoints: Subject 1 sum of fx = 2(64.5)+7(74.5)+8(84.5)+3(94.5) = 129+521.5+676+283.5 = 1610, mean = 1610/20 = 80.5. Subject 2 sum of fx = 4(14.5)+4(24.5)+5(34.5)+3(44.5)+2(54.5)+2(64.5) = 58+98+172.5+133.5+109+129 = 700, mean = 700/20 = 35. Modal class: Subject 1 = 80-89 (f = 8); Subject 2 = 30-39 (f = 5). Mode estimate by formula L + d1/(d1+d2) x w: Subject 1 = 79.5 + (1/6)(10) = 81.2 (1 dp); Subject 2 = 29.5 + (1/3)(10) = 32.8 (1 dp). Median class: Subject 1 = 80-89; Subject 2 = 30-39. Median estimate L + ((n/2 - cf)/f) x w: Subject 1 = 79.5 + (1/8)(10) = 80.75 (about 80.8); Subject 2 = 29.5 + (2/5)(10) = 33.5.

CUMULATIVE FREQUENCY (less-than upper boundaries). Subject 1: <59.5: 0; <69.5: 2; <79.5: 9; <89.5: 17; <99.5: 20. Subject 2: <9.5: 0; <19.5: 4; <29.5: 8; <39.5: 13; <49.5: 16; <59.5: 18; <69.5: 20.

OGIVE ESTIMATES (from grouped data, position n/4 = 5th, n/2 = 10th, 3n/4 = 15th). Subject 1: Q1 = 69.5 + (3/7)(10) = 73.8 (1 dp); median = 80.75; Q3 = 79.5 + (6/8)(10) = 87.0. Subject 2: Q1 = 19.5 + (1/4)(10) = 22.0; median = 33.5; Q3 = 39.5 + (2/3)(10) = 46.2 (1 dp). Estimated IQR: Subject 1 = 13.2 (87.0-73.8); Subject 2 = 24.2 (46.2-22.0).

KEY COMPARISON: Subject 1 has the higher mean (80.35 vs 33.85), higher median (80.5 vs 31.5), higher minimum (67 vs 11) and the smaller spread (range 28 vs 49). Subject 2 has the larger spread. The highest single score in Subject 1 (95) is higher than the highest in Subject 2 (60).
characters: School: a Grade 10 class of 20 learners at a day secondary school in Kisumu, near Lake Victoria. Learners are referred to as Learner 1 to Learner 20 following the order of the raw lists (individual learners may be named in examples, but must keep the scores given by that position). Subject 1 teacher: Mr. Otieno, whose class scored 67 to 95. Subject 2 teacher: Mrs. Wanjiku, whose class scored 11 to 60. Both are the same 20 learners, tested with a mark out of 100 in each subject. Head of Department / Deputy Principal: Madam Achieng, who asks the class to use the data to decide next steps. Pass mark 50 is the school's agreed pass mark for this activity. Learners' groupwork: groups of 4 present findings on manila paper. Contexts allowed for side examples: maize yields in the Rift Valley, tea picking in Kericho, daily mandazi sales in Mombasa, fish catches on Lake Victoria. These must not change the anchor data. Nothing in the data tells us WHY the learners scored differently (the difficulty of the test, teaching method and revision time are unknown), so lessons must treat reasons as hypotheses to be investigated, not facts.
outcome: After ordering, tabulating, summarising and graphing the two sets, the class finds that Subject 1 scores are high and tightly clustered (mean 80.35, median 80.5, all 20 learners pass, range 28), while Subject 2 scores are low and widely spread (mean 33.85, median 31.5, only 4 of 20 pass, range 49). The same learners therefore cannot all be 'weak'; the difference is between subjects, so decisions must be made per subject. Final recommendations: Mr. Otieno's class should continue and be given extension or enrichment work; Mrs. Wanjiku and the learners should reteach and revise the Subject 2 topics, run remedial support for the 16 learners below 50, and collect more data (for example topic-by-topic marks and a second test) to find the cause before concluding. Data organised into tables, measures and graphs shows patterns and spread that the raw lists hid, which is why collecting, organising and interpreting data supports effective decisions.
conventions: Pass mark = 50 out of 100. Call the subjects 'Subject 1' and 'Subject 2' only. n = 20 for each set. Use 'score' for each data value, x for the value or class midpoint, f for frequency, fx for frequency times midpoint, cf for cumulative frequency. Tally marks are grouped in fives. Common class width = 10, classes written 10-19, 20-29, ... 90-99 for BOTH subjects; class boundaries are x.5 values (9.5, 19.5, ..., 99.5); class midpoint = (lower limit + upper limit)/2 (e.g. 14.5 for 10-19 using limits, equivalent to boundary midpoint). Formulas: mean = sum of x / n for ungrouped data; mean = sum of fx / sum of f for grouped data; median of ungrouped data = average of 10th and 11th ordered values; grouped median = L + ((n/2 - cf)/f) x w; grouped mode = L + (d1/(d1+d2)) x w where d1 = f(modal) - f(before), d2 = f(modal) - f(after). Quartiles for ungrouped data use the median of the lower and upper halves (Q1 = median of first 10 values, Q3 = median of last 10 values); IQR = Q3 - Q1. Round exact means to 2 dp (80.35, 33.85) and grouped estimates to 1 dp, except 80.75 and 33.5 which may be shown as exact. Always say 'estimate' for measures from grouped data and note they differ slightly from the exact ungrouped values. Histogram: bars touch, drawn at class boundaries, frequency on the vertical axis. Frequency polygon: plot (midpoint, frequency) points and join with straight lines, closing to the axis at the empty classes either side. Ogive: plot (upper boundary, cf) points and join with a smooth curve or straight lines, starting at the lower boundary of the first class with cf 0. For comparing subjects, both graphs use the same classes 10-19 to 90-99 and the same axes scales. Subject 1 has frequency 0 for classes 10-19 to 50-59 and Subject 2 has frequency 0 for 70-79 to 90-99. Bimodal = two modes; Subject 1 has no mode. Do not claim causes for the score difference; use words such as 'may', 'could' and 'we need more data'.

lessonMap.focus: The Two Sets of Scores: Phenomenon Launch
lessonMap.teaches: Raw data can be arranged in ascending order to see highest, lowest and pass/fail at a glance, and the raw lists raise questions (patterns, spread, action needed) that need organising and summarising.
lessonMap.buildsOn: None (launch lesson); uses learners' prior knowledge of marks and pass/fail.
lessonMap.usesData: Both raw lists, both ascending-order lists, pass mark 50 and the pass/fail counts (20 pass in Subject 1; 4 pass and 16 fail in Subject 2); lowest, highest and range.

lessonMap.focus: Frequency Distribution Tables for Ungrouped Data
lessonMap.teaches: How to use tally marks to build an ungrouped frequency distribution table (score, tally, frequency) and check that the frequencies add to n.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 1: the ordered lists and the question that raw lists are hard to read.
lessonMap.usesData: Ungrouped frequencies: Subject 1 all scores frequency 1; Subject 2 scores 32 and 60 each frequency 2, total 20 each.

lessonMap.teaches: How to choose class width and class limits/boundaries and classify data into a grouped frequency table.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 2: ungrouped tables with Subject 1 all frequency 1 shows the need for grouping; tally skills.
lessonMap.usesData: Range (28 and 49), common class width 10, grouped frequency table for both subjects and class boundaries/midpoints.

lessonMap.focus: Mean, Mode and Median of Ungrouped Data
lessonMap.teaches: How to calculate and interpret the mean, mode and median from ungrouped data (including no mode and bimodal cases).
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 1-2: ordered lists (for the median) and ungrouped frequency tables (for the mode).
lessonMap.usesData: Ungrouped measures: Subject 1 mean 80.35, median 80.5, no mode; Subject 2 mean 33.85, median 31.5, modes 32 and 60; sums 1607 and 677.

lessonMap.focus: Mean, Mode and Median of Grouped Data
lessonMap.teaches: How to estimate the mean (using midpoints and fx), the modal class and mode, and the median from a grouped frequency table, and why these are estimates.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 3: grouped tables, boundaries and midpoints; Lesson 4: the meaning of each measure and the exact values to compare against.
lessonMap.usesData: Grouped table, midpoints, sum fx = 1610 and 700, grouped means 80.5 and 35, modal classes 80-89 and 30-39, mode estimates 81.2 and 32.8, median estimates 80.75 and 33.5.

lessonMap.focus: Representation of Data I: Histograms and Frequency Polygons
lessonMap.teaches: How to draw a histogram using class boundaries and a frequency polygon using midpoints, and to read the shape and spread of each subject.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 3: grouped table with boundaries and midpoints; Lesson 5: modal class and midpoints.
lessonMap.usesData: Grouped frequency table for both subjects on the same axes; boundaries 9.5 to 99.5; polygon points at midpoints 14.5 to 94.5 with zero frequency classes.

lessonMap.focus: Representation of Data II: Cumulative Frequency and Ogives
lessonMap.teaches: How to build a cumulative frequency table, draw an ogive and read off the median, quartiles and interquartile range as estimates.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 3: grouped table and upper boundaries; Lesson 5: grouped median formula to check the ogive reading; Lesson 6: graph-drawing skills.
lessonMap.usesData: Cumulative frequency table (e.g. Subject 2 <39.5: 13) and ogive estimates: Subject 1 Q1 73.8, median 80.75, Q3 87.0; Subject 2 Q1 22.0, median 33.5, Q3 46.2; IQRs 13.2 and 24.2.

lessonMap.focus: Interpretation of Data: Comparing Subjects and Predicting Next Steps
lessonMap.teaches: How to interpret tables, measures and graphs together to compare two sets (average, spread, shape, pass rate) and draw justified conclusions and predictions.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 4-7: measures of central tendency, histograms, polygons, ogives and quartiles; Lesson 1: pass/fail counts.
lessonMap.usesData: All the summary results: means 80.35 and 33.85, medians 80.5 and 31.5, ranges 28 and 49, IQRs, pass counts 20 and 4, and 7 learners at 40 or above in Subject 2.

lessonMap.focus: Why Collecting, Organising and Interpreting Data Leads to Effective Decisions
lessonMap.teaches: The importance of collecting, organising and interpreting data in decision-making, shown by writing evidence-based recommendations to answer the driving question and revising the final model.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 1-8: the whole sequence (ordering, tables, measures, graphs, interpretation) and the Driving Question Board.
lessonMap.usesData: The Key Comparison and the outcome: recommendations for learners, Mr. Otieno and Mrs. Wanjiku, the 16 learners below 50 in Subject 2, and further data to collect (second test, topic-by-topic marks).
